task: Prepare me for a meeting with Datadog (datadoghq.com)

merged.claim: Datadog describes itself as the leading (AI-powered) observability and security platform for the AI era, giving unified visibility across the stack to manage complexity at scale.

Olivier Pomel is Co-Founder & CEO; on the Q2 2026 call (Aug 6, 2026) he said Datadog helps customers observe, secure and act on AI workloads, builds autonomy into operations, and cited 36% YoY growth and 'the future of observability is not just observing, it's fixing.'

David Obstler is CFO; on the Q2 call he said guidance uses recent trends with conservatism, includes the largest customer's usage reduction, and emphasized acceleration elsewhere; FY2026 guidance raised to $4.45-4.47B (~30% growth); flags AI-native cohort volatility.
Alexis Lê-Quôc is Co-Founder & CTO; said Datadog invests ~30% of revenue in R&D and is unifying the 100+ DASH releases around helping customers find and fix issues.
Adam Blitzer is Chief Operating Officer.
Yanbing Li is Chief Product Officer.
Emilio Escobar is Chief Information Security Officer.
Sean Walters is Chief Revenue Officer; at the Feb 12, 2026 Investor Day he outlined a segmented go-to-market model (commercial sales for new logos, enterprise sales for complex customers).
Yuka Broderick is SVP of Strategic Finance & Investor Relations and participated in the Q2 2026 earnings call.

Priority: make Bits AI an increasingly autonomous operating layer ('AI for Datadog') for detection, investigation, remediation, development and security; Bits Code, Bits Chat and Bits Agent Builder reached GA and fully autonomous Bits AI was unveiled at DASH 2026 (June 9-10) with 100+ capabilities.

Priority: build observability and security for customers' own AI stacks and agents ('Datadog for AI') incl. AI Guard, Agent Evals/Bits Evals, Agent Console, Agent Observability, Data Observability, GPU monitoring; LLM Observability passed 1,000+ customers.

Datadog completed the Adaptive ML acquisition (RL Operations platform), announced with Q2 results Aug 6, 2026 and completed June 30, 2026, to accelerate Datadog AI Research in world models and agentic LLM post-training for observability.
Datadog introduced Scout 1.0 (Oct 15, 2026), a specialized SRE model for Bits Investigation with a lower cost profile enabling more frequent, earlier investigations; in closed preview.
Priority: grow the security business, which passed $100M ARR growing mid-40s% YoY; 8,500+ customers but only ~2% wallet share in large accounts; DASH added AI Guard and Bits Security Analyst.

Priority: expand AI-enabled security and workflow automation — Sept 3, 2026 natural-language workflows via Bits Chat, Slack and AI coding agents through the MCP Server; Sept 30 GA of AI-native SAST in Code Security (GovCloud excluded); Oct 19 programmatic security-finding severity changes via API and MCP Server.

Priority: expand data coverage and deployment flexibility, including Bring Your Own Cloud (launched at DASH 2026, starting with logs and expanding to metrics and traces), Federated Logs, Network Path, Network Configuration Management, Journey Monitoring and Infinite Cardinality Metrics.

Priority: win larger, more complex enterprise customers and scale large accounts; ~4,720 customers at $100K+ ARR as of June 30, 2026 (+23% from ~3,850); an enterprise win validated the expanded go-to-market for the world's largest companies.
Priority: build the federal and broader government business, with substantial sales investment, pipeline, and certifications for delivering SaaS to government levels.
Datadog Q2 2026 results (Aug 6, 2026): revenue $1.12B (+36% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.65, operating cash flow $316M, FCF $279M, $5.0B cash; Q3 guided $1.135-1.145B; FY guidance raised to $4.45-4.47B.
Datadog scheduled its Q3 FY2026 earnings release for November 4, 2026, before U.S. market open, with a call afterward (announced Oct 14, 2026).
Datadog was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Observability Platforms for the sixth consecutive year, and 'Company to Beat' in Gartner's August 2026 AI Vendor Race.

Challenge: largest-customer concentration and usage variability — the largest customer (unnamed; widely believed to be OpenAI, est. 5-10% of revenue) renewed with lower usage, with a reduction starting Q3 built into Q3 and full-year guidance; guidance models growth ex-largest customer at 20%+; management cautions of cloud/observability optimization.

Challenge: usage-based pricing pressure and bill unpredictability — high-cardinality metrics and per-host/per-metric billing get costly with AI/Kubernetes telemetry; Datadog responded with Infinite Cardinality packaging; Grafana Cloud, New Relic, Coralogix and self-hosted OpenTelemetry sell predictability (example: $144,000/year cut in six weeks).

Challenge: intensifying competition and platform consolidation — Palo Alto Networks closed ~$3B Chronosphere deal (Jan 29, 2026; observability ARR >$500M), Dynatrace autonomous SRE agent GA, Cisco's planned Galileo acquisition, 2026 Gartner MQ Leaders include Dynatrace, Splunk, New Relic, Elastic, Grafana; Datadog operates in a highly competitive, fast-changing market.

Challenge: keeping pace with rising AI/technology complexity and customer expectation of autonomous operations, and securing agentic workloads against prompt injection, poisoning, malicious coding-agent packages and unknown agents.
Stock fell ~15.6-17% after the Q2 2026 report on Aug 6, 2026 despite a beat, as investors wanted a larger guidance raise; traded roughly $220-268 through September 2026.

Goldman Sachs downgraded Datadog to Sell in Jan 2026 ($113 target) citing customer budget fatigue and hyperscaler bundle deflation; bear case not played out as of Sept 2026 (Grafana passed $400M ARR by Jan 2026).

Challenge: operational reliability and migration risk — US1 status page had minor incidents in Sept–Oct 2026, and the Oct 29, 2026 transition of the US1 status page to Datadog's Status Pages product may break custom integrations relying on the old URL, structure or payloads.
Challenge: growth depends on existing customers buying more and renewing, attracting new customers, and adapting to changing data privacy/security laws and regulations.
Talking point: autonomy economics tension — Bits AI remediates end-to-end while Datadog bills on ingestion/indexing/hosts; open question of how autonomy will be priced.

nimble.claim: Datadog (NASDAQ: DDOG) describes itself as the leading AI-powered observability and security platform for the AI era, giving unified visibility across applications, infrastructure, data, models and security and using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers.
Datadog's stock fell ~15.6-17% after the Q2 2026 report on Aug 6, 2026 despite a beat, because investors wanted a larger guidance raise; it traded roughly $220-268 through September 2026.

Datadog faces usage-based pricing pressure: per-host/per-metric billing gets expensive as AI and Kubernetes telemetry grows, and Grafana Cloud, New Relic, Coralogix and self-hosted OpenTelemetry stacks sell predictability and lower ingestion costs (e.g., a cloud communications company cut $144,000/year from its Datadog bill in six weeks).

Goldman Sachs downgraded Datadog to Sell in Jan 2026 ($113 target) citing customer budget fatigue and deflationary architectures from hyperscaler bundles, though the bear case had not played out as of Sept 2026 (Grafana passed $400M ARR by Jan 2026).

Datadog faces intensifying competition: Palo Alto Networks completed its ~$3B Chronosphere acquisition (Jan 29, 2026) and reports observability ARR above $500M; Dynatrace took its Autonomous SRE Agent to GA the same month Datadog unveiled autonomous Bits AI; the 2026 Gartner MQ names Dynatrace, Splunk, New Relic, Elastic and Grafana all Leaders.

Datadog has AI-native customer concentration and usage volatility risk: FY2026 guidance models growth excluding its largest customer (widely believed to be OpenAI, est. $150-300M ARR, ~5-10% of revenue) at 20%+; an in-house build would be material, and management cautions customers may optimize cloud and observability usage.

Olivier Pomel is Datadog's Co-Founder & CEO; on the Q2 2026 call he cited 36% YoY revenue growth, customers building with AI, and said 'the future of observability is not just observing, it's fixing.'
David Obstler is Datadog's CFO; he delivered FY2026 guidance raised twice to $4.45-4.47B (~30% growth), plans with conservative revenue, and flags AI-native cohort volatility and concentration.
Alexis Lê-Quôc is Datadog's CTO & Co-Founder.
Adam Blitzer is Datadog's Chief Operating Officer.
Yanbing Li is Datadog's Chief Product Officer.

Priority: Datadog is scaling fully autonomous agentic AI ('AI for Datadog'), launching Bits Code, Bits Chat and Bits Agent Builder to GA and unveiling fully autonomous Bits AI for end-to-end incident detection, investigation and remediation at DASH 2026.

Priority: Datadog is building observability and security for customers' own AI stacks ('Datadog for AI'), launching 100+ capabilities at DASH 2026 (June 9-10) including AI Guard, Agent Evals, Agent Console and GPU monitoring; LLM Observability passed 1,000+ customers.

Datadog completed its acquisition of Adaptive ML (Reinforcement Learning Operations platform) on June 30, 2026 to accelerate Datadog AI Research in world models and agentic LLM post-training for observability.

Priority: Datadog is growing its security business, which surpassed $100M ARR growing mid-40s% YoY; 8,500+ customers use security products but security is only ~2% of wallet share in large accounts; DASH 2026 added AI Guard and Bits Security Analyst.

Priority: Datadog launched Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) at DASH 2026 for deploying Datadog within customer environments, including a BYOC Log Management product, read by commentators as a concession that data wants to stay where it lives.

Datadog Q2 2026 results (Aug 6, 2026): revenue $1.12B (+36% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $0.65, operating cash flow $316M, FCF $279M, ~4,720 customers with $100k+ ARR (+23%), $5.0B cash; FY2026 guidance raised to $4.45-4.47B; Q3 guided $1.135-1.145B.
Datadog was named a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Observability Platforms 2026 for the sixth consecutive year, and 'Company to Beat' in Gartner's August 2026 AI Vendor Race.

Talking point: autonomy economics tension — Bits AI remediates end-to-end while Datadog bills on ingestion/indexing/hosts; question of how autonomy will be priced and whether it coexists with the revenue model.

Datadog challenge: keeping pace with fast-growing AI complexity and securing agentic workloads; Datadog highlighted defenses for prompt injection, poisoning, malicious coding-agent packages, and unknown agents.

Datadog challenge: competitive pressure as platform vendors consolidate observability, security, and AI-agent governance; Cisco's planned Galileo acquisition (combining Splunk's network/security position with AI-agent observability) escalates pressure on Datadog and Dynatrace.

Datadog challenge: operational reliability and migration risk; its US1 status page recorded minor delayed-events, delayed-notification, on-call, and RUM incidents in Sept–Oct 2026, and the Oct 29 status-page migration could break custom integrations relying on the old URL, structure, or payloads.

Olivier Pomel, Co-founder and CEO, said on the Q2 call that AI is accelerating customers' cloud and platform usage and that Datadog is focused on helping customers observe, secure, and act on AI workloads while building more autonomy into operations.
Alexis Lê-Quôc, Co-founder and CTO, said Datadog invests about 30% of revenue in R&D and is unifying the 100+ DASH releases around helping customers find and fix the issues that matter most.

Datadog priority: make Bits AI an increasingly autonomous operating layer for detection, investigation, remediation, development, and security workflows (monitors, root cause, fix recommendation/implementation, release validation, code fixes, test automation); launched 100+ capabilities at DASH (June 2026).

Datadog priority: build and commercialize AI-native observability and security for customers' AI stacks and agents, including Agent Console, Agent Observability, Data Observability, Bits Evals, and AI Guard.

Datadog priority: invest in specialized AI research and lower-cost, higher-frequency incident investigation, via Scout 1.0, its first model specialized for investigating production issues (closed preview with Datadog teams and selected customers).

Datadog priority: expand data coverage and deployment flexibility across cloud, on-prem, networking, databases, logs, user experience, and cost management, including Network Path, Network Configuration Management, Federated Logs, Bring Your Own Cloud for logs (expanding to metrics and traces), Journey Monitoring, and Infinite Cardinality Metrics.
Datadog priority: scale enterprise adoption and larger accounts; Q2 2026 revenue was $1.12 billion, up 36% YoY, with about 4,720 customers at ≥$100K ARR vs. about 3,850 a year earlier.

Recent change (2026-10-15): Datadog introduced Scout 1.0, a specialized SRE model for Bits Investigation, with a cost profile intended to support much more frequent, earlier investigations; in closed preview.

Recent change (2026-10-15): Datadog announced the transition of its US1 status page to its own Status Pages product, scheduled for October 29, 2026; custom integrations relying on the old URL, structure, or API payload may need updates.

Recent change (2026-08-06): Datadog reported Q2 2026 results (revenue $1.12B, +36% YoY) and highlighted Bits Code, Bits Chat, Bits Agent Builder, 100+ DASH capabilities, Adaptive ML, and its Q3/full-year outlook.

parallel.claim: Datadog, Inc. describes itself as “the leading AI-powered observability and security platform.”
Olivier Pomel, CEO & Co-Founder of Datadog, highlighted on August 6, 2026 the expanded go-to-market approach targeting the world's largest companies and continued investment in federal sales.
David Obstler, Datadog CFO, said on August 6, 2026 that guidance continued to use recent observed trends with conservatism applied to growth assumptions.

Sean Walters, Datadog Chief Revenue Officer, outlined at the February 12, 2026 Investor Day a segmented go-to-market model: commercial sales focused on new logos and enterprise sales managing more complex customers.

Datadog challenge: a customer usage reduction affected the revenue outlook; management acknowledged it on the August 6, 2026 earnings call and incorporated the (unnamed) customer's impact into guidance for the rest of 2026.

Datadog challenge: customers have long been frustrated by unpredictable bills from higher-cardinality metrics; Pomel said Datadog addressed this technically and commercially through different metrics packaging (Infinite Cardinality packaging).

Datadog priority: win larger, more complex enterprise customers; Pomel said an enterprise win validated the expanded go-to-market approach focused on the world's largest companies and competing in complex environments.

Datadog priority: build the federal and broader government business; Pomel said Datadog is investing substantially in federal/government sales, sees a pipeline, and has invested in certifications needed to deliver SaaS to different levels of government.

Datadog priority: expand AI-enabled security and operational automation, evidenced by September releases of AI-native SAST and workflows via Bits Chat and AI coding agents, and an October update extending AI-assistant control to security-finding severity.

On 2026-10-19 Datadog added the ability to change security-finding severity programmatically via a public API endpoint and the Datadog MCP Server, letting teams align findings with their environment and risk context.

On 2026-09-30 Datadog made AI-native Static Application Security Testing (SAST) generally available within Datadog Code Security, running on Datadog-hosted scans without Agent installation or upgrade; GovCloud is excluded.
On 2026-09-03 Datadog expanded natural-language workflow creation and execution to Bits Chat, Slack, and compatible AI coding agents via the Datadog MCP Server.

firecrawl.claim: Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale.
Priority: Datadog aims to help customers observe, secure, and act on AI-enabled solutions, per CEO Olivier Pomel (Aug 6, 2026).

Priority: Datadog is building autonomy into operations via AI agents and automated incident response, including fully autonomous Bits AI for end-to-end incident detection, investigation, and remediation, and Bits Agent Builder for custom AI agents.
Priority: Datadog is investing in AI research (world models and agentic LLM post-training for observability), including via the Adaptive ML acquisition.
Priority: Datadog is expanding adoption among larger enterprise customers, with about 4,720 customers at $100,000+ ARR as of June 30, 2026, up 23% from about 3,850 a year earlier.

Priority: Datadog is strengthening AI and cloud security and customer-controlled deployment, with AI Guard (protecting agents from prompt injection and poisoning) and Bring Your Own Cloud announced at DASH 2026.
Challenge: Datadog must manage rising technology complexity while customers increasingly expect autonomous operations.
Challenge: Securing AI agents against new attack modes such as prompt injection and poisoning, an active security problem around AI adoption.
Challenge: Datadog operates in a highly competitive, rapidly changing market and must adapt to changing data privacy and security laws, regulations, and contractual obligations.
Challenge: Datadog's growth depends on existing customers buying additional subscriptions and renewing, and on attracting new customers.
Recent event: On Oct 14, 2026 Datadog scheduled its Q3 fiscal 2026 earnings release for November 4, 2026, before U.S. market open, with a conference call afterward.
Recent event: Datadog acquired Adaptive ML to accelerate Datadog AI Research work on world models and agentic LLM post-training for observability (announced Aug 6, 2026).

Recent event: Datadog announced more than 100 new capabilities at DASH 2026, including autonomous Bits AI, AI Guard, Bring Your Own Cloud, and Bits Agent Builder; Bits Code, Bits Chat, and Bits Agent Builder reached general availability.

Key person: Olivier Pomel is CEO & Co-Founder of Datadog; on Aug 6, 2026 he said customers use Datadog to observe, secure, and act on AI solutions and that Datadog helps them manage complexity and build autonomy.
Key person: Alexis Lê-Quôc is CTO & Co-Founder of Datadog.
Key person: Yanbing Li is Chief Product Officer of Datadog.
Key person: Adam Blitzer is Chief Operating Officer of Datadog.
Key person: Emilio Escobar is Chief Information Security Officer of Datadog.

c1.note: The Q2 2026 release (Aug 6, 2026) calls Datadog 'the leading observability and security platform for the AI era' and mentions unified visibility across the stack; I read a syndicated copy because the investor-site page returned 403.

c2.note: Pomel's title, the 36% YoY growth, and his quotes on helping customers manage complexity, observing, securing and acting on AI, and building autonomy are confirmed; the exact 'fixing' line was not found in any source I could read, so that part is unconfirmed.

c3.note: Obstler's title, the $4.45-4.47B FY guidance, conservatism in guidance, and the largest-customer usage reduction already in guidance are confirmed by the release and call coverage; the ~30% growth figure and the AI-native cohort volatility remark were not directly seen.

c4.note: Lê-Quôc is CTO and co-founder, and the 30% R&D / 100+ DASH launches quote is real, but it dates from DASH on June 9, 2026, about 134 days ago and outside the 90-day window.

c5.note: The leadership page lists Adam Blitzer as Chief Operating Officer; this is a title only, with no recent statement or action attached.

c6.note: The leadership page lists Yanbing Li as Chief Product Officer.

c7.note: The leadership page lists Emilio Escobar as CISO.

c8.note: Sean Walters is confirmed as CRO and presented at the Feb 12, 2026 Investor Day. I could not retrieve the slides or transcript to confirm the segmented go-to-market detail, and the event is outside the 90-day window.

c9.note: Transcripts show Yuka Broderick opened the Aug 6, 2026 Q2 call. They give her title as SVP of Investor Relations, so 'Strategic Finance' is unconfirmed. The leadership page does not list her.

c10.note: Datadog launched 100+ capabilities at DASH on June 9, 2026, and Bits AI is positioned as autonomous, with new modules including Code and Chat. I found no source confirming GA status for Bits Code, Chat or Agent Builder. The event is about 4 months old, so it falls outside the 90-day window, though the priority is still current.

c11.note: The cited PDF returned 403 and an empty fetch. AI Guard and the DASH AI launches are confirmed, but I found no source for the 1,000+ LLM Observability customers. The Q2 call and release don't mention it.

c12.note: The Aug 6, 2026 Q2 release lists the Adaptive ML acquisition for AI Research, with about $101.7M cash paid for acquisitions in the quarter. The release gives no close date. Search results say the deal was announced June 30, which is outside the 90-day window, so only the Aug 6 disclosure falls inside it.

c13.note: The blog post is dated Oct 15, 2026. It describes Scout 1.0 powering Bits Investigation in closed preview, with 3–19x lower estimated inference cost than comparable models.

c14.note: The leadership page has none of the $100M security ARR, mid-40s% growth, 8,500 customers or 2% wallet share figures. The Q2 release and call transcript don't have them either. AI Guard is confirmed, but the Bits Security Analyst claim is not.

c15.note: The release notes confirm AI-native SAST GA on Sept 30 (not in GovCloud) and the Oct 19 severity override via API and MCP Server. I could not confirm the Sept 3 natural-language workflows entry, because the page was too long to read in full.

c16.note: Search results for TechTarget and the Aug 2026 call confirm BYOC (logs, with metrics and traces coming), Federated Logs and Infinite Cardinality Metrics. I could not open the transcript or TechTarget text myself, and I found no confirmation of Network Path, Network Configuration Management or Journey Monitoring.

c17.note: The Q2 8-K confirms about 4,720 customers at $100K+ ARR, up 23% from about 3,850. I did not confirm the enterprise-win and go-to-market claim because I could not read the call transcript.

c18.note: The Q1 call (May 7) confirms FedRAMP High and expanded public-sector go-to-market. That is outside 90 days, and I could not read the Q2 transcript to confirm the cited federal pipeline and sales-investment remarks.

c19.note: The Q2 8-K confirms every figure: revenue $1.12B (+36%), non-GAAP EPS $0.65, operating cash flow $316M, FCF $279M, $5.0B cash, Q3 guidance $1.135-1.145B and FY guidance $4.45-4.47B. Reported Aug 6, which is within 90 days.

c20.note: Search results confirm the Oct 14 announcement of a Nov 4 release before market open, with an 8:00 a.m. ET call. I could not open the investor page directly because it returned 403.

c21.note: Datadog's blog dated Sep 14, 2026 confirms the 'Company to Beat' report (Aug 19, 2026). The sixth-year Leader placement was announced Jul 15, about 98 days ago, so it is slightly outside the 90-day window.

c22.note: In the Aug 6, 2026 Q2 call, the largest customer renewed but cut usage from Q3 and guidance was derisked. The stock fell 19%. The customer's identity as OpenAI is analyst speculation, and I did not verify the specific '20%+ ex-largest customer' figure.

c23.note: Infinite Cardinality Metrics is real, and third-party posts criticise Datadog's cost. I could not confirm the competitor-driven framing, the $144,000 example or the date. The cost complaints are also long-standing, not new.

c24.note: Palo Alto closed Chronosphere on Jan 29, 2026 (about $3B). Cisco announced Galileo on Apr 9, 2026 and Futurum says it raises pressure on Datadog. Both events fall outside 90 days, so this is a background challenge, and I did not check the Dynatrace agent GA or the Magic Quadrant leader list.

c25.note: The DASH launch of 100+ capabilities on Jun 9, 2026 is real and framed around AI complexity and attackers using AI. The investor page returned 403, and I found nothing on prompt injection or malicious packages. The launch is also about 134 days old, outside the 90-day window, and the item describes a product theme more than a visible pain.

c26.note: The Aug 6, 2026 post-Q2 drop of about 17% (some outlets say up to 21%) despite a beat and raised guidance is confirmed. I did not verify the $220-268 September trading range, and the cause was also reported as lower usage from the largest customer and a slower Q3 outlook.

c27.note: Aggregators show Goldman assumed coverage at Sell with a $113 target on Jan 12, 2026, which is not a downgrade. It is also outside the 90-day window, and I found no support for the budget-fatigue rationale or the Grafana $400M ARR claim.

c28.note: The Oct 29, 2026 US1 status page move to Datadog's own Status Pages, with possible breakage of custom integrations, is confirmed. The page shows no incidents from Oct 7 to Oct 21, so the incident claim is unsupported. It is a routine maintenance notice and a weak 'challenge'.

c29.note: The page returned 403 and my fetch.py attempt turned up none of the risk language. Even if present, this is generic forward-looking boilerplate, not a visible company-specific challenge.

c30.note: Datadog bills Bits AI SRE in AI Credits, about 6.5 credits per autonomous investigation, so pricing is not purely ingestion-based. The talking point is analyst inference, not a sourced fact. Its premise that autonomy pricing is open is partly contradicted by that credit pricing.

c17.note: Q2 2026 release (Aug 6, 2026, SEC 8-K) confirms about 4,720 customers at $100K+ ARR, up 23% from about 3,850. The release has no enterprise-win quote; that part likely comes from the earnings call and I didn't check it.

c19.note: 8-K and call transcript confirm all figures: $1.12B revenue (+36%), non-GAAP EPS $0.65, OCF $316M, FCF $279M, $5.0B cash, Q3 guide $1.135-1.145B, FY guide $4.45-4.47B. Reported Aug 6, 2026, so within 90 days. I confirmed the levels but not that FY guidance was 'raised'.

c21.note: Datadog announced it was a Leader in the 2026 Magic Quadrant for the sixth straight year on Jul 15, 2026, just outside the 90-day window but still its current standing. Gartner named it Company to Beat in its Aug 19, 2026 AI Vendor Race research, inside the window.

c27.note: The Goldman downgrade to Sell ($113 target, Jan 12, 2026) did happen, but it is about 9 months old, well outside the 90-day window. Grafana's $400M ARR was announced Sep 30, 2025. I found 'budget fatigue' and 'hyperscaler bundle deflation' only in secondary sources, not in Goldman's note. Goldman kept its Sell rating in May with a $139 target.
